reply.title: Squashing Values with the Logistic Curve
reply.story: When modeling probabilities or neural networks, we often need to take any number from negative infinity to positive infinity and squash it neatly into a range between zero and one. Early biometricians studying population growth noticed that growth starts exponential but tapers off as it hits a carrying capacity. This smooth, S-shaped transition is captured by the logistic function. By adjusting the steepness parameter, we can control how rapidly the curve transitions from zero to one around the midpoint.
reply.cardDescription: Explore how the logistic function maps any real input into a range between 0 and 1. Adjust the steepness $k$ to see how the S-shaped curve transforms.
reply.instructions: Adjust the steepness slider to change how fast the curve transitions. Observe the marker output update instantly.
